response.message: I've drawn a first Google Cloud design: synthetic users sign in through Identity Platform, and a Cloud Run assistant keeps each user's conversations in Firestore and calls a Gemini model on Vertex AI with limited context. Escalations go to a human reviewer through Pub/Sub, and the first local test uses a fake model that returns scripted replies, including a simulated outage, so it can check sign-in rules, per-user isolation, size limits, outage recovery, deletion and escalation but not real Gemini quality, access, quotas or regional availability. Which country do the synthetic conversation data need to stay in, so we can choose a deployment region?

proposal.title: Authenticated conversational assistant on Google Cloud (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: an authenticated chat assistant for synthetic users with per-user conversation state, a Vertex AI model runtime, bounded context and a human escalation path. It takes no external actions. Assumptions: the region is not selected yet; Gemini model access, quotas and regional availability have not been verified; the graph shows intended design only and does not prove access rules, deployment or model quality. Native Terraform generation for this workload is not available yet, so engineering is still required.

data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: Synthetic test users chat through a browser. This is a client reference and is not provisioned.

data.label: Identity Platform
data.description: Signs in synthetic users and issues ID tokens. Cloud Run verifies each token, and the user ID in the token decides which conversations the user can access.

data.label: Assistant app (Cloud Run)
data.description: Serves the chat UI and API. It rejects requests without a valid token. Its internal modules build bounded context (a maximum number of turns and bytes, plus a maximum output token count), give a recoverable fallback reply with retry if the model fails or times out, delete conversations on request, and publish an approved context snapshot for escalation. It takes no external actions.

data.label: Conversation store (Firestore)
data.description: Stores conversations under users/{uid}/conversations. Only the Cloud Run service account can access the store, and the app filters every query by the verified user ID. Deleting a conversation removes the conversation and its messages.

data.label: Gemini on Vertex AI
data.description: Model runtime that the app calls with its service account. The model version, regional availability and quota are not verified yet. The local test replaces this with a scripted mock.

data.label: Escalation topic (Pub/Sub)
data.description: Carries escalation events that hold the approved conversation context snapshot. Delivery is at least once, so events carry an idempotency key, and a dead-letter topic is planned.

data.label: Human support reviewer
data.description: Person who receives escalated conversations. The handling tool for this person is not decided yet.

data.label: Cloud Logging & Monitoring
data.description: Records request, denial, model-error and escalation metrics and sends alerts. Logs must not contain the content of conversations.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If conversation data leaks between users, the isolation guarantee is broken.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: One user cannot read another conversation.
requirementDrafts.statement: A user can read, list or delete only their own conversations, and a request for another user's conversation is denied.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Size limits control cost, delay and how much data is exposed.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Context and response sizes are bounded.
requirementDrafts.statement: The prompt context and the model response each have a configured maximum size. Requests above the limit are trimmed or rejected.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Model failures must not lose conversation state or end the session.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Model outage produces a recoverable response.
requirementDrafts.statement: If the model times out or fails, the user gets a recoverable reply and the conversation is kept.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Stored context must not remain after a user deletes a conversation.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Deleting a conversation removes its stored context.
requirementDrafts.statement: Deleting a conversation removes its stored context and messages.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without the context, the reviewer cannot continue the case.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Escalation retains the approved conversation context.
requirementDrafts.statement: An escalation sends the approved conversation context to a human reviewer and keeps it available to that reviewer.

Act as a patient architecture consultant and teacher. Start with the exact evidence state. If blocked before checks, explicitly say runtime tests have not run and the design is not yet validated. An empty failures list NEVER means a sound, complete or correct design. Celebrate only named checks that actually passed. Explain the most important remaining issue in plain language and help the user make progress. Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result.
